ONE_LINE_DESCRIPTION: Push an existing GitHub SSH remote from Git Bash using an explicit HTTP CONNECT proxy
TRIGGER_CONTEXT_HINT: asks to push existing commits to GitHub over SSH
ENVIRONMENT_HINT: using Git Bash on Windows with a reachable local HTTP CONNECT proxy
COMPATIBILITY: git >=2.40, OpenSSH, connect with -H support, an authorized SSH key
SHELL: Git Bash; commands below use Bash syntax
NETWORK: Example HTTP CONNECT proxy at 127.0.0.1:7890; verify actual protocol and port
TOOLS: git, ssh, connect with HTTP CONNECT support
ENVIRONMENT_WHY: The SSH transport needs its own proxy command. Git http.proxy config applies to HTTP(S), not SSH. This example illustrates corrected commands; it is not a newly observed successful network run.
TRIGGER_1: push these commits to GitHub over SSH
TRIGGER_2: upload this project using the existing GitHub SSH remote
TRIGGER_3: use an HTTP CONNECT proxy for this SSH push
TRIGGER_4: 把提交通过 SSH 推到 GitHub
TRIGGER_5: check the proxy before pushing this branch to GitHub
QUICK_START_COMMAND_2: branch=$(git symbolic-ref --quiet --short HEAD) && git rev-parse --verify HEAD &&
QUICK_START_NOTE: Prerequisites: origin has exactly one GitHub SSH push URL; the current branch has commits; the SSH key is authorized; connect supports -H; the proxy supports HTTP CONNECT to the SSH endpoint. Check the actual protocol/port first. The chained quick start stops on failed prerequisites. Review any first-use host key against GitHub published fingerprints. This example does not create a repository or change remote URLs.
STEP_1_TITLE: Inspect the existing remote and proxy helper
STEP_1_WHY: Inspect the actual push URL, not only the fetch URL. Continue only with one GitHub SSH destination and a connect helper supporting -H (HTTP CONNECT). The quick start chains prerequisites with && so failures prevent pushing. HTTPS needs a different proxy/authentication workflow. Do not assume connect is installed.
STEP_2_TITLE: Read the actual current branch and confirm a commit exists
STEP_2_COMMAND: branch=$(git symbolic-ref --quiet --short HEAD) && git rev-parse --verify HEAD
STEP_2_WHY: Stop on failure. A detached HEAD or branch without commits needs attention before pushing. Branch names may be main, master or something else; Git Bash does not choose them.
STEP_3_TITLE: Push using an explicit SSH ProxyCommand
STEP_3_WHY: The SSH command receives the HTTP CONNECT proxy explicitly for this operation. Git http.proxy does not configure SSH. A SOCKS-only proxy requires a different helper option and must not be used with -H.
BAD_APPROACH_1: Set git http.proxy and assume an SSH remote is proxied
WHY_FAILS_1: HTTP(S) proxy configuration does not configure the SSH transport
FAIL_SYMPTOM_1: SSH still attempts a direct connection; a timeout alone does not prove the cause
BAD_APPROACH_2: Run git push origin main or master without checking the branch
WHY_FAILS_2: The named local ref might not exist, or the branch might have no commits
FAIL_SYMPTOM_2: src refspec does not match any
BAD_APPROACH_3: Treat a successful ls-remote as proof the push uploaded this commit
WHY_FAILS_3: Reading remote refs only proves read access; the expected ref and commit must match
FAIL_SYMPTOM_3: Remote query succeeds while the intended branch is absent or points at an older commit
VERIFY_COMMAND: remote=$(git remote get-url --push --all origin) && test "$(printf '%s\n' "$remote" | wc -l)" -eq 1 && branch=$(git symbolic-ref --quiet --short HEAD) && local_oid=$(git rev-parse HEAD) && remote_oid=$(GIT_SSH_COMMAND="ssh -o ProxyCommand='connect -H 127.0.0.1:7890 %h %p'" git ls-remote --exit-code "$remote" "refs/heads/$branch" | cut -f1) && test "$local_oid" = "$remote_oid" && printf "Verified: remote branch matches local HEAD\n"
EXPECTED_OUTPUT: Verified: remote branch matches local HEAD (exit 0); missing or different commits fail the check
ADDITIONAL_NOTES: Illustrative fixture, not a verified personal experience. Stop after a failed prerequisite. Confirm the helper, SSH key, proxy protocol/port and endpoint in the current environment. Do not claim an HTTP proxy fixes SSH without an explicit transport configuration. Do not switch authentication methods merely because a previous attempt failed; diagnose the actual error.
